title: InvokeServer Yields (and can hang)
summary: InvokeServer pauses the calling thread until the server's OnServerInvoke returns. If that handler errors, yields forever, or is unset, your client thread is stuck — often silently. Wrap in pcall, set expectations.

explanation.whatItIs: Asking a question and waiting for the answer — with no built-in timeout. The waiting IS the feature; the danger is waiting forever.
explanation.whyItExists: Request/response needs synchronization; yielding is the simplest correct implementation.
symptoms: UI never appears after an InvokeServer line
'Works after touching something' — a later event resumed unrelated threads while yours stayed parked
No error at all — just nothing happening afterwards
explanation.fix: pcall the invoke; keep OnServerInvoke handlers fast, non-yielding, and error-free; prefer events when you don't truly need the answer immediately.
tips: Server handlers that yield (WaitForChild forever etc.) park every caller
Never InvokeClient — same hang risk plus exploiters control the reply
commonMistakes: OnServerInvoke set in a script that errored earlier → unset → instant return of nil? Actually unset InvokeServer errors; debug the server script first
Invoking in loops thinking it's cheap — each is a round trip
No fallback path when invoke fails

examples.title: Defensive invoke
examples.code:
-- ❌ Silent hang risk:
-- local data = remote:InvokeServer()
-- setupUI(data)   ← never runs if invoke hangs

-- ✅ Guarded:
local ok, data = pcall(function()
    return remote:InvokeServer()
end)

if ok and data then
    setupUI(data)
else
    warn("Data fetch failed — using defaults")
    setupUI(getDefaultData())
end
